instruction: We act for Zeisein Lift Services, Inc., an elevator maintenance and modernization contractor, on its supply agreement with Bruben Elevator Components, LLC. Please review all seven documents in the folder and send me a memo listing each issue you find. For each one, give the document and section where it appears, explain why it matters for Zeisein, and recommend a fix. Keep it practical so I can use it with the client.

rubric.text: The response finds that the exclusivity clause makes Bruben the exclusive source of all Elevator Components for Zeisein and its Affiliates throughout North America. It finds this far broader than the deal in the Order Form, which covers only hydraulic power units, valve units and controller boards for the Mid-Atlantic program in Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Delaware. It places the issue in Supply Agreement Section 3.1. It explains why this matters to Zeisein and recommends a fix.

The response finds that the Service Level Schedule's narrow definition of 'Critical Part' (only parts listed in Annex 1) controls over the Supply Agreement's broad definition. It concludes that the 4-hour emergency dispatch commitment and service credits cover only the listed parts. It places the issue in Supply Agreement Section 1.4 or Service Level Schedule Section 1.2. It explains why this matters to Zeisein and recommends a fix.

The response finds that the liability cap carve-out for 'obligations under any Order Form' takes Zeisein's site indemnity in the Order Form outside the cap. It concludes this leaves Zeisein with uncapped liability for site claims, including claims caused by Bruben. It places the issue in Supply Agreement Section 12.2 or Order Form Section 6. It explains why this matters to Zeisein and recommends a fix.

The response finds that Zeisein's September 14, 2026 objection to the price increase was sent after the 30-day objection window closed, measured from Bruben's July 28, 2026 Price Adjustment Notice. It concludes that Bruben may treat the increase as deemed accepted. It places the issue in Zeisein's September 14, 2026 letter or Supply Agreement Section 5.3. It explains why this matters to Zeisein and recommends a fix.
The response states that the Service Level Schedule prevails over the body of the Supply Agreement in the order of precedence.
The response is presented as a memo that sets out the issues as separate, distinguishable items.
The response claims that Zeisein's September 14, 2026 objection to the price increase was timely under the Supply Agreement.
The response claims that the Order Form limits or narrows the exclusivity obligation in Supply Agreement Section 3.1.
hints: exclusivity limited by the Order Form
